title: Embedding variant safety matrix and delta gating for rerank compatibility
creator: Asha Raman
description: Problem: New embedding variants are added frequently and we lack an automated, tenant-aware gate that ensures reranker compatibility (quality delta) while preserving latency SLOs. Current rollouts are manual, rely on coarse metrics, and produce surprises for downstream rerank pipelines and customers.
goals: 1) Define a deterministic safety matrix for embedding variants that encodes compatibility with existing rerankers and index formats. 2) Implement automatic delta-based gating that blocks or stages traffic when semantic quality regressions exceed configurable thresholds. 3) Add tenant-scoped rollout controls and graceful fallback to safe variants. 4) Surface per-tenant quality and latency signals in Console and runtime telemetry so PMs and SREs can make data-driven decisions.
acceptance_criteria:
- Safety matrix data model defined and stored in metadata service.
- Automated pre-rollout offline checks (cosine delta, recall@k on canonical evalsets) pass for at least 90% of tenants or mark tenants as excluded.
- Runtime gate enforces traffic split and prevents >5% relative drop in rerank recall for guarded tenants during canary.
- Latency budget enforcement: 95th token latency change <= 10ms for impacted endpoints.
- Console shows per-variant quality deltas, tenant impact, and rollout state.
- An operator can abort a rollout and automatically pin tenants back to previous variant.
- Security review completed and KMS access validated for model metadata updates.
rollout_plan: 1) Offline evaluation: run canonical eval sets + tenant sample against candidate variant and base variant; compute absolute and relative deltas for recall@k and NDCG.
2) Safety matrix classification: tag variant as BACKWARD_COMPATIBLE | NEUTRAL | INCOMPATIBLE by rules (format compatibility, vector dim, normalization, embedding stability).
3) Staged canary: start at 1% traffic, tenant-ranged: first internal tenants, then low-risk customers, automated 24hr monitoring window.
4) Delta gating: if rerank.recall_at_10.delta < -0.03 (relative) for any tenant AND sustained for 30min, pause and rollback that tenant.
5) Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% with automated health checks and manual sign-off for high-impact tenants.
6) Deprecation policy: mark old variants with deprecate window 90 days, provide migration helpers and migration metrics for tenants.
test_plan: Unit tests for safety matrix rules and metadata mutations.
Integration test: simulate tenant traffic through canary harness with injected quality regressions and latency changes.
E2E: verify Console displays gating state and per-tenant deltas; verify rollback flow completes within 5 minutes.
Load test: run throughput at 2x expected peak with candidate variant and assert no degradation in batching efficiency or memory blowups.
notes: Design trade-offs: centralized safety matrix simplifies reasoning but risks single point of misclassification; we will keep a per-tenant override list and audit log.
We chose a relative delta threshold strategy instead of absolute because tenants have heterogeneous datasets and baseline quality varies widely.
Consideration for quantized variants: vector dimensionality and quantization noise must be included in safety rules (e.g., quantized dims must match, or variant is INCOMPATIBLE).

Related artifacts: Confluence design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Embedding+Variant+Safety+Matrix, GitHub prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/embedding-rollouts/pull/247
